scenarios.topic: Change impact and installed network policy
scenarios.title: Stage a controller rollout with a pilot port
scenarios.summary: Restore approved desk access in stages and keep a shared reserve port outside the rollout.
scenarios.objective: Authorize access between both signed-off dispatch desks and the supplied dispatch service. Verify a controller-managed pilot before changing the other desk. Reconcile and check the completed rollout. Preserve the intake scanner’s original settings and its separation from dispatch. Keep the visitor network separate.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the exact failed result, inspect the current rationale or path, then try again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: A direct device edit changes one port immediately. The controller keeps its desired profile. A later reconciliation in this network restores the settings from that profile.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: Every port bound to a changed profile can inherit that change. A preview shows the ports affected, so you can compare them with the approved work order before applying anything.
guide.action: Make and inspect the guided change.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: A pilot is one approved device you change and test first. Confirm it reaches the service and that the reserve port remains unchanged. Then roll out the approved profile to the other device and reconcile again.
guide.action: Check the independent traffic and policy.

scenarios.explanation: A dedicated service binding keeps the approved scope narrow. The pilot confirms one working port before the other moves. Reconciliation confirms that the controller can maintain the desired configuration.
hints: Read the ports listed in the Preview. The intake profile is shared by approved desks and a reserved device.
A direct edit can look correct until Reconcile. Check which source supplies a profile after reconciliation.
An approved desk must work while the other approved desk is still in its original state to verify the pilot.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded local port settings, shared controller profiles and an explicit reconciliation rule over a supplied Ethernet topology. No actual vendor controller, API transport, rollout service, switch access or network is used.

scenarios.topic: Change impact and installed network policy
scenarios.title: Trace intent through installed policy and transport
scenarios.summary: Restore an approved fabric exchange by correcting controller intent, installing it and repairing the transport path.
scenarios.objective: Allow branch-to-office and office-to-branch traffic in the desired and installed policy. Restore the supplied service uplink and verify actual transport in both required directions. Keep the monitor-to-branch exchange working and the monitor-to-office exchange excluded.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the exact failed result, inspect the current rationale or path, then try again.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: The underlay is the routed network between the supplied edges. The overlay is a logical relationship between edge applications. Two edges need working underlay transport before an allowed overlay exchange can reach its destination.

guide.title: Try the separate example
guide.why: An application sends a northbound request to the controller. The controller stores its desired policy. A southbound update sends the resulting rule to the devices. An accepted request and an installed rule describe different points in this sequence.
guide.action: Make and inspect the guided change.

guide.title: Complete the independent assignment
guide.why: The control plane decides which traffic can pass and the data plane applies the installed rules when moving traffic. Check desired intent, installed rule and underlay result separately. Check the needed return direction and leave other exchanges unchanged.
guide.action: Check the independent traffic and policy.

scenarios.explanation: The controller keeps separate desired and installed rules. The required exchanges need an installed permit and a working underlay in the supplied virtual fabric. Independent monitor trials preserve the established boundary.
hints: An accepted request changes desired policy first. Publish it to change the installed rules.
Use the path result to separate a blocked overlay exchange from a broken physical-side route.
Read both monitor rows before applying a broad rule.
scenarios.simplifications: A supplied IPv4 transport graph, explicit virtual policy requests and a bounded installed rule table. No real signaling, paths outside the inventory, overlay protocol, encapsulation or underlying switch/controller platform is implemented.
